observations: Photo 0: Used automotive alternator, dusty/grimy casing, cooling fins visible, electrical connector and pulley partly obscured, lying on concrete floor.
Photo 1: Same alternator from rear/pulley end, showing fan blades, pulley hub, and mounting ears with bolt holes.
Photo 2: Side view showing ribbed pulley, wiring connector port, and casing wear/corrosion on housing.
No brand, part number, or vehicle fitment markings are legible in any photo.
Watermark 'U-ZION LINKS AUTO'S' overlaid on all images; no additional context given.
No photo shows the unit powered on, spinning, or tested with a meter.

claims.claim: Also deals on all kinds of car spare parts

risks.risk: Alternator may not function (no output, worn brushes, bad bearings)
risks.proof: Video clip of unit spinning on a bench test rig with voltage reading on a multimeter

risks.risk: Unknown vehicle make/model/engine fitment, affecting resale value and compatibility
risks.proof: Clear photo of part number/casting number stamped on housing, or seller statement of exact vehicle application with visible match
risks.if_unproven: priced as generic unidentified-fitment alternator, lower tier

risks.risk: Pulley or clutch pulley condition (freewheel pulleys can be seized or slipping)
risks.proof: Close-up photo/video of pulley being manually spun by hand
risks.if_unproven: priced assuming pulley may need replacement

risks.risk: Internal corrosion or water damage not visible from outside casing
risks.proof: Photo of internal rotor/stator or regulator removed from housing
risks.if_unproven: priced as risk of internal damage, worst case

proof_requests: Photo of any part/casting number stamped on the alternator body
Video of the alternator being spun on a test bench showing voltage output
Statement and photo match of which vehicle make/model/year this was pulled from
Close-up of electrical connector pins for corrosion or damage
response.reason: The item is clearly identifiable by type as a used, untested car alternator with no verifiable brand, model, or vehicle fitment, so it must be priced at worst case as an unverified, non-working, generic-fitment unit pending further proof.
